messages.author: 8ae1efaa2cf53fab
messages.subject: Possible problem with sfit/cfit?
parts:
Hi,

I have been running multiple 6.0 comparisons, which have been working
perfectly, until now.
Working with 55 arrays, following the standard workflow (re the 6.0
page):


> print(acc);
AllelicCrosstalkCalibration:
Data set: XXX
Input tags:
User tags: *
Asterisk ('*') tags: ACC,ra,-XY
Output tags: ACC,ra,-XY
Number of files: 55 (3622.45MB)
Platform: Affymetrix
Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
Algorithm parameters: (rescaleBy: chr "all", targetAvg: num 2200,
subsetToAvg: chr "-XY", flavor: chr "sfit", alpha: num [1:5] 0.1 0.075
0.05 0.03 0.01, q: num 2, Q: num 98)
Output path: probeData/XXX,ACC,ra,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6
Is done: FALSE
RAM: 0.00MB
> csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose);

20080903 16:58:02| Array #1 ('1a11a10a2007') of 55...done
20080903 16:58:02| Reading all probe intensities...
20080903 16:58:04| Reading all probe intensities...done
20080903 16:58:04| Fitting calibration model...
20080903 16:58:04| Allele basepair #1 ('AC') of 6...
20080903 16:58:04| Fitting...

then

20080903 16:58:04| Flavor: sfit
/home/laviniag/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/2.7/sfit/bin/cfit:
unrecognized option `--flavor'
63
cfit [ options ] k [ data [ weight ]]

Fit a simplex with k vertices to points in the file <data> (stdin
is used if not supplied).

<weight> is a file of point weights (if not supplied, w_j = 1/n).

-h, --help this help
-v, --verbose dump progress to stderr

-i, --Minit <filename> initial simplex
-d, --dump <int> dump mode (0 none, 1 final, 2 each alpha, 3
each REX)
-M, --outM <filename> where M is dumped [ stdout ]
-X, --outX <filename> where X is dumped

-a, --alpha <num,num,...> comma- or space-separated sequence of alpha
-T, --maxiter <int> maximum number of REX steps
-f, --frobratio <num> ratio of ||DM||/||M|| (inner loop
convergence)
--QRtolerance <num> ratio of ||q_i||/||q_1|| (QR termination)

-C, --constraints <int> 0 none, 1 nonnegative, 2 box, 3 probability-
like
-x, --lubox <lb,ub> lower and upper bound in box constraints
(specifying this turns on --constraints 2).
If this
is not specified, the dimension-specific
lower and
upper bounds are read from a file `lubox'
containing
2 x m matrix of lower- and upper-bound
vectors.

-o, --origin <filename> origin vector, offset data by this vector
[default 0]
-g, --gamma <num> `eye-height' in projective transform [default
0]
-u, --viewdir <filename> `viewing direction' vector [ meanY/(meanY^T
meanY) ]
--u_1T u = (1,1,1,... )
-D, --denom_weight use the denominators as observation weights
--outPY <filename> save the transformed Y into this file
--outPM <filename> dump projective-transformed M (according
to the dump mode option).

-q, --chopless <num> assign zero weight to points if u^T y is
less
-Q, --chopmore <num> or more than the specified percentiles.

-R, --robust <num> robust coefficient (if compiled with -
DWITH_ROBUST)
Error in read.table(pipe(cmd), colClasses = colClasses, quote = "",
comment.char = "") :
no lines available in input
20080903 16:58:04| Fitting...done
20080903 16:58:04| Allele basepair #1 ('AC') of 6...done
20080903 16:58:04| Fitting calibration model...done
20080903 16:58:04| Calibrating 55 arrays...done
20080903 16:58:04|Calibrating data set for allelic cross talk...done

which clearly leads to

> print(csC);
Error in print(csC) : object "csC" not found

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.7.0 (2008-04-22)
x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu

locale:
LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8;LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8;LC_MONETARY=C;LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8;LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8;LC_NAME=C;LC_ADDRESS=C;LC_TELEPHONE=C;LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8;LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
base

other attached packages:
[1] aroma.affymetrix_0.9.4 aroma.apd_0.1.3
R.huge_0.1.6
[4] affxparser_1.12.2 aroma.core_0.9.4
sfit_0.1.5
[7] aroma.light_1.8.1 digest_0.3.1
matrixStats_0.1.3
[10] R.rsp_0.3.4 R.cache_0.1.7
R.utils_1.0.4
[13] R.oo_1.4.5 R.methodsS3_1.0.3
>

I did downloadPackagePatch in case I had missed a recent patch.

With thanks for your time,

Lavinia Gordon.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Possible problem with sfit/cfit?
parts:
Hi,

my bad. This bug arrived with a patch I uploaded Aug 31. I didn't
pay attention to some side effects, so I have undone that patch again.
Update the patch with:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

and see if it works.

Cheers

Henrik
